\[
I_{\text{out}}(p) = \frac{\sum_{q \in \Omega_p} w(p,q)\, I(q)}{\sum_{q \in \Omega_p} w(p,q)},
\qquad
w(p,q) = e^{-\frac{\lVert p - q \rVert^2}{2\sigma_s^2}}\; e^{-\frac{d(G(p),\, G(q))^2}{2\sigma_r^2}}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(G\): The guide image
- \(I\): The image to filter
- \(\sigma_s, \sigma_r\): The spatial and range sigmas
- \(\Omega_p\): The disk-shaped window around p

The same weighted mean as the bilateral filter, but the value weight compares the guide G at the two pixels, not the image. Where the guide has an edge, neighbors across it get almost no weight, even if the image is too noisy to show that edge. The difference d is that of the guide luma, or the distance between guide colors. With the image itself as the guide and the color difference, this is the bilateral filter in its color mode.
